status_summary: H.R. 421, the Small Business Regulatory Flexibility Improvements Act, introduced 2025-01-15 and referred to the House Judiciary, Small Business and Oversight committees (the Judiciary Committee ordered it reported 13 to 12 on 2025-06-10, with no later action recorded), would replace the panel provisions of 5 U.S.C. 609 so that any agency, not only the currently covered agencies, must notify the Chief Counsel for Advocacy before proposing a rule with a significant small business impact, and it adds judicial review and a first-time paperwork fine waiver. A Senate bill of the same name, S. 5178, was introduced 2026-07-30 and referred to the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee. No 119th Congress bill titled the IMPROVE the SBA Act and no Administration statement supporting either measure was found.

timeline.event: H.R. 421, the Small Business Regulatory Flexibility Improvements Act (Representative Cline), was introduced and referred to the Judiciary, Oversight and Government Reform, and Small Business committees; it would extend the pre-proposal panel process under 5 U.S.C. 609 to agencies generally.
The House Judiciary Committee held a markup of H.R. 421 and ordered it reported in the nature of a substitute by a recorded vote of 13 to 12.
S. 5178, the Small Business Regulatory Flexibility Improvements Act (Senator Rick Scott), was introduced and referred to the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee.
